extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent practitioners, applicants, and patent examiners handling application formalities
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing submission (or omission) of drawings, entitlement to a filing date, responses to OPAP notices, petitions, and correspondence-address requirements for U.S. patent applications (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings not strictly required for filing date (post-Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications other than design applications filed on or after December 18, 2013, although drawings are not required in order to receive a filing date, drawings should be submitted on filing if necessary for the understanding of the invention because no amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are necessary for understanding, submit them on filing; otherwise an application can still receive a filing date without drawings for non-design apps filed on/after 12/18/2013. Consider the prohibition on adding new matter when deciding whether to omit drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inspection to determine necessity of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed without drawings are initially inspected to determine whether a drawing is referred to in the specification, and if not, whether a drawing is necessary for the understanding of the invention (35 U.S.C. 113 first sentence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP/examiner assesses spec references and whether drawings are necessary to understand claimed subject matter; if necessary, filing date entitlement and follow-up notices are handled as described in MPEP §601.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories where drawings usually not necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO practice treats applications with at least one process/method claim, composition applications, coated articles/products, articles made from a particular material/composition, laminated structures (only order of layers), or articles whose sole distinguishing feature is presence of a particular material as usually not requiring drawings under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: coated sheet where invention is the coating only; article distinguished solely by use of a particular hydraulic fluid; packaged sutures where package structure is conventional. If claims involve significant structural/arrangement details, drawings may still be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of applications filed without drawings that refer to drawing figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application (filed prior to 12/18/2013) or a design application having at least one claim, or a provisional application having at least some disclosure, that describes drawing figures in the specification but is filed without drawings will be treated as an application filed without all of the drawing figures referred to in the specification (see MPEP §601.01(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications will be processed only if they contain something that can be construed as a written description; OPAP will take further action (e.g., Notice of Incomplete Application) if drawings are necessary for understanding under 35 U.S.C. 113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Center may require drawings (reconsider filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appropriate Technology Center determines that drawings are necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence), the filing date issue will be reconsidered by the USPTO in nonprovisional applications filed prior to December 18, 2013 or in design applications; the application will be returned to OPAP for mailing of a 'Notice of Incomplete Application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A TC determination that drawings are necessary triggers formal steps and may affect filing date entitlement for affected application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) to establish drawing submission or non-necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with the petition fee asserting that (A) the drawing(s) at issue was submitted, or (B) the drawing(s) is not necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 for a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be accompanied by sufficient evidence (e.g., date-stamped postcard receipt) to establish entitlement to the requested filing date. For some older filings, specific oath/declaration rules apply (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63/1.64).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to submit drawings and accept later filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatively, applicant in a nonprovisional application may submit drawing(s) and accept the date of such submission as the application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of omitted drawings and accepting the later filing date is tantamount to filing a new application; consider filing a new application as a cost-effective alternative in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of inadvertent omission where omitted drawings fully contained in prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: If omitted drawing(s) was inadvertently omitted and the omitted drawing(s) is completely contained in the prior-filed application (e.g., foreign, provisional, international), applicant may submit the omitted drawing(s) by amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.57(b) (where allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendment must be identified as pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b) and comply with 1.57(b) and 1.121; application will maintain the filing date of the original deposit if requirements are met. See MPEP §217 for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application special rule: petitions asserting drawings unnecessary usually unpersuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: In design applications, petitions under 37 CFR 1.53(e) asserting that drawings are unnecessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 for a filing date will not be found persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will mail a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' for design apps lacking required drawings; applicant must promptly file petition showing drawings were submitted or promptly submit drawings and accept the submission date as the filing date (with pre-9/16/2012 oath/declaration rules where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP Notice of Omitted Items when drawing figures referenced are missing
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP reviews papers to determine whether all figures of the drawings mentioned in the specification are present. If an application (under 35 U.S.C. 111 prior to 12/18/2013, or a design app) is filed without all drawing figures referred to in the specification, and the application contains something that can be construed as a written description (and other minimal items), an OPAP notice (e.g., 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)') will be sent indicating the application has been accorded a filing date but is lacking some figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after 12/18/2013 under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (c), an OPAP notice will be sent if drawings are lacking but the application contains something that can be construed as a specification, with or without claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after OPAP mailing in nonprovisional applications (A: establish prior receipt)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant asserting that the drawing(s) was in fact received with the application must, within two months from the date of the OPAP notice, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with the petition fee and evidence of deposit; the petition fee will be refunded if it is determined the drawings were received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. Provide documentary evidence (e.g., date-stamped receipt) to support prior receipt claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after OPAP mailing in nonprovisional applications (B: submit omitted drawings and request later filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit the omitted drawings in a nonprovisional application and accept the date of such submission as the application filing date by filing any omitted drawing(s) and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the petition fee within two months of the OPAP notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before 9/16/2012, omitted drawings must be filed with an oath/declaration per pre-AIA rules. Two-month period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. Submission + petition under 1.182 asks the Office to accept omitted items and accord the date of submission as the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after OPAP mailing in nonprovisional applications (C: accept application as deposited by amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may accept the application as deposited in the USPTO by filing an appropriate amendment (e.g., substitute specification excluding claims, replacement drawing sheets renumbered, or amendment relying on incorporation by reference) without adding subject matter that was in the omitted drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepting as deposited, the application will maintain the original filing date. Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121(d), 1.121(b)(3), and 1.125, and must not add new matter (35 U.S.C. 132(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and treatment of provisional applications with omitted drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not grant petitions under 37 CFR 1.182 to accept omitted drawing(s) and accord an application filing date as of the date of such submission in provisional applications; applicants should file a new completed provisional application instead. Failure to timely respond to OPAP notice for a provisional application results in acceptance as deposited and eventual automatic abandonment at end of pendency if complete under 37 CFR 1.51(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional apps, the OPAP notice permits either establishing prior receipt via petition under 1.53(e) or accepting as deposited by failing to file a petition within a two-month non-extendable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely reply to OPAP notice leads to abandonment (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications in which an OPAP notice regarding omitted items has been mailed will be retained in OPAP to await a reply. Failure to timely reply to the OPAP notice in a nonprovisional application will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response is required (two-month period, extendable in certain cases) to avoid abandonment; timely-completed nonprovisional apps are forwarded to Technology Center for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction requirement for figure numbering/lettering mismatches
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings include figures labeled with number-letter combinations (e.g., Fig.1A, 1B, 1C) but the brief description of the drawings refers only to Figure 1 (without letters), this is an error in the specification which must be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will require correction; ensure brief and detailed descriptions reference the exact figure labels shown in drawings to avoid correction/amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when application is entitled to a filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is entitled to a filing date, the examiner should notify applicant of the omission in the next Office action and require applicant to either (A) accept the application as filed without the drawing figures (with required amendments), (B) file any omitted drawing figure(s) and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the later filing date, or (C) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) alleging the drawing figure(s) were in fact deposited on filing (with supporting evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's Office action should set forth the options and the required amendments or petitions to be filed in response; petition fees and documentary requirements apply as noted elsewhere in MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements if applicant accepts application as filed without figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant accepts the application as filed without all of the drawing figures referred to in the application, applicant is required to submit: (1) an amendment to the specification canceling all references to the omitted drawing figure(s) including any reference numerals shown only in the omitted drawing figure(s); (2) an amendment with replacement sheets of drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) to renumber the drawing figures submitted on filing consecutively (if necessary); and (3) a further amendment to the specification correcting references to correspond with relabeled drawing figure(s), both in the brief and detailed descriptions of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not add the subject matter that was in the omitted drawing(s) or otherwise add new matter (35 U.S.C. 132(a)); submit in response to the Office action and follow 37 CFR 1.121/1.125 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: If application not entitled to filing date because drawings necessary and absent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines that the application (filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) prior to 12/18/2013 or a design application) is NOT entitled to a filing date because the application does not contain any drawing figure and at least one drawing figure is necessary under 35 U.S.C. 113 (first sentence), the examiner should forward the application to OPAP for mailing of a 'Notice of Incomplete Application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forwarding to OPAP triggers the incomplete-application process and possible abandonment if not remedied; this is distinct from situations where a filing date is accorded despite missing figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney must include full mailing address and contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: The attorney’s or agent’s full mailing address (including ZIP Code) must be given in every power of attorney. The telephone and fax numbers of the attorney or agent should also be included to facilitate prompt delivery of communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §402.02 for detailed information and relevant forms. For applications filed before certain dates, different rules/forms may apply (see referenced MPEP subsections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address requirement and change rules (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must specify a correspondence address to which the Office will send notices, letters, and other communications. The correspondence address must either be in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or in a clearly identifiable manner elsewhere in any paper submitted with an application filing. The Office should be promptly notified of any change in correspondence address, and the change should be provided in a manner calling attention to it; mere inclusion of a different address in a paper for another purpose would not ordinarily be recognized as an address change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first-named inventor as the correspondence address. If multiple addresses are given, the Office will select one (may prefer Customer Number-associated address). A daytime telephone number is requested. Only parties authorized by 37 CFR may change the correspondence address; changes in continuing applications require explicit identification of the correspondence address to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign and who may change correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity under §1.34; or (3) the applicant (§1.42). The correspondence address may be changed by parties set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(3); prior to appointment of any power of attorney, a patent practitioner named in the application transmittal papers acting in a representative capacity may change the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner named only in letterhead is not considered named in transmittal papers for purposes of changing the correspondence address; a clear identification of the individual as a representative is required. For juristic entities, papers must be signed by a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of correspondence address discrepancies and hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one correspondence address is specified (in a single paper or multiple papers), the Office will select one of the specified addresses for use as the correspondence address and may select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address. The hierarchy provided in 37 CFR 1.76(d) governs inconsistencies between an ADS and other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office does not select the correspondence address actually desired by applicant, it will not re-mail papers to the desired address; ensure ADS and other papers are consistent. For e-filings, an acknowledgment is sent to the submitter but a correspondence address must still be set forth in ADS or a paper.
